newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIA MAY BID FOR 2004 EUROPEAN CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIA MAY BID FOR 2004 EUROPEAN CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Russia aims to bid to stage the European soccer championship finals in 2004, Russian Football Union (RFS) officials said on Wednesday.
"We will definitely fight for the right to host the 2004 European championship," RFS president Vyacheslav Koloskov was quoted as saying by Sport-Express newspaper.

RFS director-general Vladimir Radionov confirmed a bid was being considered but stressed much preliminary work still needed to be done. "It is simply our great wish to hold the European championship in Russia," he said.

Koloskov said he was sure that by 2004, Russia, whose sports facilities have been badly run down since the collapse of the Soviet Union, would have the six to eight world-class stadiums needed to host such an event.

Three months ago, Koloskov flatly denied reports he was considering a bid for the 2006 World Cup finals, saying crisis-hit Russia had no hope of building enough international stadiums in time for that larger event.

Koloskov said Russia wanted to stage the final of a European club competition in the near future, following the completion this September of a multi-million dollar upgrade to Moscow's Luzhniki Olympic stadium.

Russian officials boast that the 100,000-seat arena, now fitted with a retractable roof, will be second only to the Maracana in Rio. But the country has no other large stadium to compare with modern western standards. Second city St Petersburg failed in a bid this year to host the 2004 Olympic Games.
European soccer's governing body UEFA is expected to make a decision on bids for the 2004 championships next year.
Spain is considered a leading contender while Austria and Hungary are planning a joint bid. The 2000 finals will be held jointly in Belgium and the Netherlands.
